citation: Hayes et al. (2017), Tectonic Summaries of Magnitude 7 and Greater Earthquakes from 2000 to 2015, USGS Open-File Report 2016-1192
evidence_used: Event-specific tectonic summaries for M7+ Japan-Kuril-Kamchatka megathrust, outer-rise, and deep-slab events from 2000 through 2015 (including 2003 M8.3 Tokachi-oki, 2006 M8.3/2007 M8.1 Kuril doublet, 2011 M9.1 Tohoku-oki, and 2013 M8.3 Sea of Okhotsk).
limitations_and_caveats: Excludes post-2015 M7+ events (such as 2024 M7.5 Noto Peninsula and 2025 M8.8 Kamchatka).

citation: Hasterok et al. (2022), New Maps of Global Geological Provinces and Tectonic Plates, Earth-Science Reviews 231, 104069
evidence_used: Subplate overlays across Kuril-Kamchatka (79), Okhotsk (14), Pacific (10), Southwest Japan Inner (6), Amur (5), and Kinki Outer (4).
limitations_and_caveats: 2D surface polygons assign deep NW-dipping Pacific slab events beneath Sea of Okhotsk/Japan to Okhotsk/Amur.

citation: Bird (2003), An updated digital model of plate boundaries, Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 4(3), 1027
evidence_used: Plate boundary discretization across Pacific, Okhotsk, Amur, and Philippine Sea plates.
limitations_and_caveats: Surface boundary discretization only; does not represent 3D Pacific or Philippine Sea slab contours.

citation: Hayes et al. (2018), Slab2, a comprehensive subduction zone geometry model, Science 362(6410), 58-61
evidence_used: 3D slab geometry reference separating Kuril-Kamchatka-Japan Pacific slab from Nankai Philippine Sea slab.
limitations_and_caveats: Regional 3D slab context; individual event mechanisms require ComCat detail product verification.
